description:
**Monday Immune Engager** — our weekly pick from the latest immune-engager digest.

**[Aberrant expression of HERV-K envelope in lymphoma represents an opportunity for novel treatments](https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-25-1542)**

*Molecular Cancer Therapeutics, 2026*

DOI: [10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-25-1542](https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-25-1542)

**Question:** Does HERV-K (HML-2) envelope mark clinically relevant DLBCL states, and is it a usable surface target?

**Answer:** HERV expression mirrors the ABC/GCB split but adds nothing independent of cell of origin, and Env reaches the surface of only 2 of 8 lines; a humanized VHH-Fc, FF-01, drives NK killing and internalizes, with no Env-negative control in the 3D assay and no in vivo data.

**Three takeaways**

1. Discarded multi-mapping reads split ~340 DLBCLs into 4 survival-distinct clusters mirroring ABC/GCB; not offered as prognostic.
2. Env was detected by qPCR in 8 of 8 lines, by immunoblot in 5, on the surface in 2; every functional result rests on RCK8.
3. FF-01 (Kd 142 nM, peptide 3) gave ~2.7x ADCC signal at 6 h, NK killing in 2D and 3D, and ~1.5-fold selective internalization.

source_metadata.abstract:
Abstract
                  Purpose: Human endogenous retrovirus K (HERV-K/HML-2) is a human-specific endogenous retrovirus family that maintains intact open reading frames and is aberrantly expressed in multiple cancers. We tested whether HERV-K, specifically its envelope (Env) protein, marks clinically relevant diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) states and serves as a tractable immunotherapeutic target. Experimental Design: Locus-level transposable element (TE) and HERV expression was quantified in two independent DLBCL RNA-seq cohorts using curated TE annotation and a uniform alignment/counting workflow. Env transcript and protein expression (including cell-surface localization) was validated in lymphoma cell lines using RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, and flow cytometry. Functional relevance was assessed by siRNA-mediated Env knockdown. Candidate extracellular linear epitopes were predicted in silico and synthesized for serological and phage display assays. Anti-Env camelid VHHs were isolated, humanized, and tested for binding, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), and antigen-dependent internalization. Results: TE transcripts stratified DLBCL into clinically distinct subgroups, and high HERV-K expression associated with an interferon/viral-mimicry program. Env RNA was detected in patient tumors and cell lines, and the protein was detected on the surface of a subset of lymphoma cell lines, in which Env knockdown reduced proliferation. A humanized heavy-chain antibody (FF-01) bound surface Env, induced selective ADCC in Env-positive models (reporter and primary NK-cell assays), and underwent rapid antigen-dependent internalization. Conclusions: HERV-K activity identifies biologically meaningful DLBCL states and exposes a targetable surface antigen. FF-01 provides proof of principle for antibody-based strategies against HERV-K Env, including ADCC- and ADC-oriented approaches.
